title: The Borrowed Verdict
corpus_scope: ICLR 2018–2026 · 8,439 papers · every meta-review unit matched to the reviewer unit it most resembles
question: Where does the area chair's language in a meta-review come from — near-copy, echo, or their own words — and whose voice gets echoed?

figures.title: What the meta-review is made of
figures.deck: 73% of meta-review reasoning is the area chair's own words; 0.5% is near-copy. But criticism is borrowed more than praise — at every cutoff.

claims.statement: 73% of meta-review reasoning is the area chair's own words; 0.5% is near-copy.
claims.derivation: own = 0.7306 → 73%; copy = 0.0047 → 0.5%, share of meta-review units by cosine-similarity tier to their nearest reviewer unit

claims.statement: Criticism's borrowed edge reaches 6.6 points past praise's, and the gap survives any cutoff (+7.0 / +6.6 / +3.3 at similarity thresholds of 0.70 / 0.75 / 0.80).
claims.derivation: borrowed-mass (copy+echo) share for criticism minus praise meta-units, recomputed at similarity cutoffs 0.70/0.75/0.80; at the 0.75 default, negative meta units echo reviewers at 28.8% against 22.4% for positive ones

figures.title: When the AC borrows, from whom
figures.deck: Echoes concentrate on one reviewer (60% from a single voice), and in rejections they lean to the harsher side of the panel, 60/40.

claims.statement: On papers with three or more echoed units, 60% of echoes come from a single reviewer.
claims.derivation: share of echo-tier meta units on multi-echo papers (≥3 echoed units) attributed to the single most-echoed reviewer
claims.verified: claim recomputed from source island; source_path corrected from who[], 2026-08-26

claims.statement: The most-echoed reviewer is the panel's uniquely lowest rater in 16% of cases against 13% for the uniquely highest.
claims.derivation: ACECHO.echoed_position.lowest and .highest, among the 3,334 panels with full, non-unanimous rating panels; in half of panels the echoed reviewer's rating ties an extreme

claims.statement: In rejections, echoes lean to the harsher side of the panel, 60/40; accepts do not (51/49, interval crossing even).
claims.derivation: share of echoes attributed to the harsher-than-mean side of the panel, split by decision, among the 2,220 decided rejections and 752 accepts where the echo-weighted rating differs from the panel mean
claims.verified: claim recomputed from source island; source_path corrected from who[], 2026-08-26

caveats.text: Nearest-neighbor attribution measures textual proximity, not causal influence: an area chair and a reviewer may both independently echo the paper itself rather than one echoing the other.
